questions.q: The first major opposition from the religious authorities resulted in the arrest of Peter and John. What public miracle performed by them triggered this arrest? (Acts 3-4)
options: Turning stones into bread at the temple gates
Raising a young girl from the dead in the marketplace
Healing a man lame from birth at the Beautiful Gate of the temple
Calling down fire from heaven on a Roman soldier
questions.explain: Peter and John healed the lame beggar in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. The resulting crowd and Peter's preaching disturbed the priests and the Sadducees, leading them to arrest the apostles (Acts 4:1-3).

questions.q: Who is recorded in the book of Acts as the first Christian martyr, executed for his bold defense of the gospel before the council? (Acts 7:54-60)
questions.explain: Stephen, one of the seven deacons, gave a powerful historical defense of the faith before the Sanhedrin. Enraged by his words, the council dragged him out of the city and stoned him to death, making him the first Christian martyr.

questions.q: During the stoning of Stephen, the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man who aggressively persecuted the early church. What was his name before his conversion?
questions.explain: Acts 7:58 mentions, "Then they cast him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul." Saul later became known as Paul after his conversion.

questions.q: In Acts 9, Saul was on his way to arrest Christians when he was surrounded by a light from heaven and fell to the ground. To which city was he traveling?
questions.explain: Saul approached the high priest and asked for letters to the synagogues at **Damascus**, so that if he found any belonging to the Way, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem (Acts 9:1-2).
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 1 (Paper 2)

questions.q: About that time, King Herod laid violent hands upon some who belonged to the church. Who did he kill with the sword, making him the first apostle to be martyred? (Acts 12:1-2)
questions.explain: Acts 12:1-2 records: "About that time Herod the king laid violent hands on some who belonged to the church. He killed James the brother of John with the sword."
